question.text: Ms. Priya Shah, CIO of Aravalli Long-Short Fund (a Cat III AIF), is explaining to a junior analyst why hedge-fund style investments are classified as 'alternative' rather than 'traditional' under the Chapter 2 framework. Which single ESSENTIAL characteristic most distinguishes alternative investments from traditional investments?

answer.text: Illiquidity — alternatives are generally not readily convertible to cash, being off-market or complex structures without a ready market
Alternatives necessarily offer higher absolute returns than listed equity in every cycle
Alternatives are compulsorily regulated by RBI rather than SEBI
Alternatives are restricted only to retail investors with ticket sizes below INR 1 lakh

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 2.1, the ESSENTIAL characteristic of alternative investments is 'illiquidity' — they are not readily convertible into cash because they are either off-market investments or complex structures lacking a ready secondary market. Traditional investments (listed equity, bonds, MF/ETF units) are defined by LIQUIDITY via the capital-market trading mechanism. The Trap: Option B is a half-truth — alternatives SEEK higher returns but do not always deliver, and this is not the definitional characteristic. Option C is plainly wrong — AIFs (including Cat III) are SEBI-regulated under the AIF Regulations 2012. Option D inverts reality — AIFs are meant for sophisticated/HNI investors with a minimum ticket of INR 1 crore, not retail. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C (All-Cat Manager) tests the same traditional-vs-alternative taxonomy. XIX-A/B (Distributor exams) stress suitability screening for illiquid alternatives. XXI-B (Portfolio Manager) deals with LIQUID listed securities, so the illiquidity dimension is less central there. Manager's Pro-Tip: At a Cat III desk the illiquidity dimension is usually addressed via side-pockets for stressed names and a gating/notice-period architecture. Even though the fund NAV is struck daily and the strategy may be largely liquid long-short, your LPA must give you the side-pocket option so one illiquid 'fallen-angel' position does not destroy daily NAV integrity for continuing investors.
